messages:
samir: Quick roundup from the Vanguard dedicated outage postmortem — consolidating follow-ups and owners. Root cause still tied to intermittent VPC peering state flaps + an edge on‑prem NAT rule that dropped connections under specific SYN bursts.

maria: thanks. can you list the concrete action items and owners? want to make sure we don't leave anything ambiguous. :eyes:

samir: yep — high level first: (1) isolation detection improvements, (2) peering stability hardening, (3) onprem NAT rule audit & fix, (4) runbook + automation for faster remediation, (5) recurrence analysis to catch pattern. assigning owners below.

ash: i can take peering hardening (2) and run the synthetic peering tests. proposing 2-week window for patches and 1-week for rollout canary.

liam: i'll own the detection improvements (1). plan: add a heartbeat + divergence detector on the control plane and emit an isolation alert when tenant routes deviate > 3s from expected. timeline: prototype in 5 days, deploy in staging 9 days.

ana: i'm on the NAT rule audit (3). already started gathering iptables/nft snapshots from the affected rack. found one rule that had a conditional match that could drop mid-flow when conntrack table neared 80% — could be the trigger.

samir: specific tasks and tickets: 
- ASH-1012 (ash): peering kernel param tune + retries + backoff. target: patch branch by 2026-04-05.
- LIAM-1999 (liam): control-plane divergence detector + alert. target: staging prototype 2026-03-28.
- ANA-527 (ana): NAT rule audit + remediation PR. target: PR by 2026-03-25.
- SAMIR-320 (samir): update dedicated isolation runbook, add a triage checklist + scripted remediation steps. due 2026-03-30.
- OPS-automations (ash + liam): add automatic peering rollback job that triggers when >2 peering resets in 10m for a tenant. initial automation by 2026-04-01.

maria: please add the Jira links once created and tag the customer success lead so Vanguard sees an action timeline. also add a note about temporary mitigations we applied (increased conntrack, temporary peer hold).

samir: created the postmortem doc here: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PM-2347 (postmortem). will link follow-up tickets to that.

devops-bot: new issue created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ASH-1012 by ash.

ash: quick note on tests — i'll build a small continuous traffic harness that simulates SYN bursts and route churn. code stub: 
```
# run in harness
ab -n 10000 -c 50 http://vanguard-test.lb/health
sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 handle 1: root netem loss 0.1% delay 50ms
```

ana: found the nft rule line: `ip saddr 10.8.0.0/16 ct state established counter packets 0 jump accept` — looks like one conditional was constructed assuming conntrack gc would keep up. adding explicit conntrack timeout tuning + alert when table >70%.

liam: recurrence analysis — my quick scan of historical incidents shows small flaps on peering after major config pushes 3 of 6 times in last 90 days. pattern: config rollout + heavier traffic window => higher risk. we should schedule peering canaries after any peering-related config push.

samir: agreed. add rollout gating: canary in a single AZ for 1 hour with synthetic traffic, then expand. add a preflight script that validates conntrack headroom.

maria: who will own coordination with Vanguard on scheduled maintenance windows? need to align before we run canaries.

ash: i can coordinate with CS for a maintenance slot. recommend a window next Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC to avoid peak for their region.

samir: runbook changes (excerpt to add): 
- Step 1: verify tenant isolation via control-plane divergence detector.
- Step 2: escalate to peering-runbook (owner: ash).
- Step 3: apply conntrack headroom increase (+30%) if conntrack >70% (owner: ana).
- Step 4: if peering resets >2 in 10m, trigger automated rollback to last known-good peering config and alert SRE oncall.

liam: adding metric names to the runbook: `net.peering.resets`, `controlplane.route-divergence-ms`, `conntrack.usage_pct`. alerts: severity P1 when resets>2 in 10m for any single tenant.

maria: also add a customer-facing blurb for CS: short summary + ETA for fixes, and promised follow-ups at 48h/7d/14d.

samir: on recurrence: i'm going to run a small SQL query across incident tags to surface correlated deploys and traffic spikes, will post results by EOD tomorrow. if we see deploy linkages, we add preflight gating to our deployment pipeline for peering-related changes.

devops-bot: reminder: weekly remediation backlog sync scheduled for 2026-03-26 16:00 UTC.

ana: i've opened ANA-527 with remediation steps + PR link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ANA-527. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/nat-fixes/pull/42.

ash: created ASH-1012 branch and draft PR: https://git.redwood.ai/serving/peering-fixes/pull/8. tests pass locally. planning canary config next.

liam: LIAM-1999 is in the backlog; created a minimal alerting rule here: https://redwood.monitoring/alerts/LIAM-1999. prototype pushed to staging.

samir: next steps: everyone paste final ticket IDs in this thread, I'll compile into the postmortem follow-up table and ping CS. also we should decide on an owner for long-term recurrence analysis (quarterly review).

maria: assign quarterly recurrence review to platform reliability — owner: samir? or nominate someone from research?

samir: i'll take initial quarter review; if heavy, we'll hand to research.

liam: small UX ask for runbook: include exact CLI snippets for rolling back peering and for verifying KV cache on the runtime after rollback. will add to the PR.

samir: thanks all. final TL;DR in one line: owners and tickets done, 2-week fix window for peering + NAT fixes, runbook + automation by next month, weekly sync added.

maria: :thumbsup: adding CS lead @olivia to keep Vanguard in the loop.

jira-bot: comment added to PM-2347: "Follow-ups linked: ASH-1012, LIAM-1999, ANA-527, SAMIR-320".

samir: closing the thread — will post consolidated follow-up sheet by EOD and set reminders on the tickets. if anyone needs to reassign, edit the Jira owner and ping here.

ana: ack.

ash: ack.

liam: ack.

maria: ack.
